cues.en: This is Los Altos Hills, a wealthy suburban town of 8,500 people in the San Francisco Bay Area that was in the news a few years ago over its fight with navigation app Waze. Los Altos Hills was one of many suburbs across North America concerned that Waze was sending too much outsider traffic through their quiet residential streets. People here and elsewhere tried a variety of tactics, from requesting the company remove certain streets, to putting up signs prohibiting through traffic, to banning certain turns during rush hour.
cues.zh: 这里是洛斯阿尔托斯山，旧金山湾区一个富裕的郊区小镇，有 8,500 人。几年前，它因与导航应用 Waze 的争斗登上新闻。洛斯阿尔托斯山是北美众多郊区之一，这些郊区担心 Waze 让过多外来车流穿过他们安静的住宅街道。这里和其他地方的人们尝试了各种办法：从要求公司移除某些街道，到竖立禁止过境交通的标志，再到在高峰时段禁止某些转弯。

cues.en: In some cases, residents fabricated reports of traffic accidents on the app to send a signal that their neighborhood is closed. On one hand, all of this is understandable. Cars are dangerous, loud, and they pollute. Having a lot of traffic for your neighborhood degrades your quality of life in meaningful ways, including threatening your kid's ability to be independent and play outside. Residents on certain roads that saw sharp increases in traffic reported being afraid to cross the road to get their mail. On the other hand, it's hard not to notice a certain contradiction.
cues.zh: 在某些情况下，居民会在应用上伪造交通事故报告，以此发出信号，表明他们的社区已封闭。一方面，这一切都可以理解。汽车危险、吵闹，还会污染环境。社区车流量大，会实实在在地降低你的生活质量，包括危及你孩子独立活动和在户外玩耍的能力。一些道路的车流量急剧增加，那里的居民表示，他们害怕过马路去取邮件。另一方面，也很难不注意到某种矛盾。

cues.en: At the same time that they're fighting to keep other people's traffic away from their neighborhood, Los Altos Hills is literally built to generate traffic for other neighborhoods. There's no grocery store within the borders of this 9 square mile or 23 square kilometer town. In fact, there are very nearly no stores at all, and this is not by chance. Los Altos Hills has a complete ban on commercial properties, meaning the only retail in town is a bookstore on a college campus and a gift shop at a monastery. Residents must travel elsewhere to buy essentially anything.
cues.zh: 就在他们努力阻止别人的车流进入自己社区的同时，Los Altos Hills 从规划上却恰恰是在为其他社区制造车流。这座小镇面积 9 平方英里、合 23 平方公里，边界内没有一家杂货店。事实上，这里几乎完全没有商店，而这并非偶然。Los Altos Hills 全面禁止商业地产，这意味着镇上唯一的零售店，是大学校园里的一家书店和修道院里的一家礼品店。居民几乎买任何东西都得出镇。

cues.en: And with its inconsistent sidewalks and close to zero transit, when residents leave they're almost always driving. The town plan mentions its dependence on the rest of the Bay Area for stores and employment, but assures that the relationship isn't one-sided because the town has a lot of natural beauty that other Bay Area residents can move there to enjoy or admire from afar. If there's anything we've learned following urban planning and city politics, it's that questioning the role of cars and cities really strikes a nerve.
cues.zh: 而且这里人行道断断续续，公共交通几乎为零，居民出门时几乎总是开车。镇规划提到，小镇在商店和就业方面依赖湾区其他地区，但保证这种关系不是单向的，因为小镇拥有大量自然美景，湾区其他居民可以搬来享受，或远远欣赏。如果说我们关注城市规划和城市政治学到了什么，那就是：质疑汽车在城市中的角色，真的会触动敏感神经。

cues.en: When you talk about the downsides of cars, from noise to safety to pollution, or support policies that give less space and priority to cars, from pedestrian streets to bike lanes to transit priority corridors and traffic calming, you're accused of waging a war on cars and attacking people's basic freedoms. We've seen this on our own channel when we talk about bikes and transit, and we saw this when living in Montreal under Bear Valerie Plant, who is constantly accused of being anti-car for pedestrian streets and new bike infrastructure.
cues.zh: 当你谈论汽车的弊端——从噪音、安全到污染——或者支持少给汽车空间和优先权的政策，从步行街、自行车道到公交优先走廊和交通稳静化措施，你就会被指责对汽车开战、攻击人们的基本自由。我们在自己的频道里聊自行车和公交时见过这种指责，住在蒙特利尔、在市长 Valérie Plante 治下时也见过——她一直因步行街和新的自行车基础设施被指责反汽车。

cues.en: Before that, we lived in Toronto under suburban mayor Rob Ford when he and his brother Doug Ford, then City Counsellor but now Premier of Ontario, were the ones denouncing the war on cars fought by the downtown elites. Car advocacy group Get Toronto Moving highlights anti-car environmentalism like bike lanes, transit signal priority, and no idling signs.
cues.zh: 在那之前，我们住在多伦多，当时是来自郊区的市长 Rob Ford 治下；他和弟弟 Doug Ford——时任市议员、现任安大略省省长——正是谴责市中心精英对汽车发动“战争”的人。汽车倡导团体 Get Toronto Moving 突出强调反汽车的环保主义，比如自行车道、公交信号优先和禁止怠速标志。

cues.en: Everyone seems to frame this debate as the anti-car urbanites versus the pro-car suburbanites, but we think this is a big misunderstanding, and not just because we know lots of people in the suburbs with more urbanist views who want better bike and transit infrastructure. Even the stereotypical suburbanites who happily drive everywhere are well aware of the downsides of cars and willing to implement policies and designs that manage and limit cars in their own neighborhoods.
cues.zh: 大家似乎都把这场争论说成是反汽车的城市人对抗支持汽车的郊区人，但我们认为这是个很大的误解，不仅因为我们认识很多住在郊区、持更城市化观点、希望有更好的自行车和公交基础设施的人。即便是刻板印象中乐于开车去任何地方的郊区居民，也很清楚汽车的缺点，并愿意在自己社区实施管理和限制汽车的政策与设计。

cues.en: We saw this with the example of Los Altos Hills at the beginning, which fought its own war against cars from the Waze app, but it's way more than just one rich town's feud with a technology company. Avoiding car traffic around your home is a part of the suburban dream, built into the design of the suburbs in fundamental ways. One of the most distinctive features of post-war North American suburbia and one of the most desirable locations for a suburban house is a cul-de-sac. Real estate ads mention them prominently.
cues.zh: 我们在开头 Los Altos Hills 的例子中看到了这一点：它曾与 Waze 应用带来的车流打过一场自己的仗，但这远不止一个富裕小镇和一家科技公司的恩怨。避开自家周围的交通，是郊区梦的一部分，从根本上融入了郊区的设计。战后北美郊区最鲜明的特征之一，也是郊区住宅最理想的位置之一，就是 cul-de-sac（尽头路）。房地产广告会重点宣传这一点。

cues.en: And studies have found that cul-de-sacs can increase the property value of a house by 10, 20, and even 30%. People like living on cul-de-sacs for the traffic safety and equality of life. People don't like tons of traffic whizzing by their front door, especially suburban families who appreciate it as a natural place for children to gather and play. People also appreciate the lack of noise from motors, car stereos, and horns. It's easier to sleep.
cues.zh: 研究发现，尽头路能让房屋价值提升10%、20%，甚至30%。人们喜欢住在尽头路，因为交通安全、生活品质均衡。人们不喜欢大量车流从门前呼啸而过，尤其郊区家庭更喜欢它作为孩子自然聚集玩耍的场所。人们也喜欢没有发动机、车载音响和喇叭的噪音。睡觉也更容易。

cues.en: It's hard to see the suburbs as entirely for the freedom of cars when their basic road layout, including cul-de-sacs, courts, and other circuitous designs, is meant to limit and discourage traffic. It's not just road layouts. Suburban-style zoning that bans shops and businesses in residential neighbourhoods is usually justified with the worry about traffic, and traffic comes up all the time as a reason to ban denser housing. In the suburbs, traffic is actually a really big deal, and avoiding it is one of the top priorities for residents.
cues.zh: 很难把郊区看作完全是为了汽车的自由，因为其基本道路布局——包括死胡同、庭院路和其他迂回设计——本意就是限制并阻碍交通。不只是道路布局。郊区式分区禁止在住宅区开设商店和企业，通常给出的理由是担心交通；而交通也一直是被用来反对更高密度住房的理由。在郊区，交通实际上是个大问题，避开交通是居民最优先考虑的事项之一。

cues.en: Part of the constant concern about traffic is people not wanting congestion slowing down their trips, but part of it is also not wanting their quiet, safe, pleasant street overrun by a bunch of new cars or trucks. Minimizing the impact of cars is even built into the basic design of suburban housing. A common justification for large suburban front lawns and houses being 10 or more meters from the sidewalk is to put you further away from any traffic that does go through your neighborhood, for the noise and the possibility of a car crashing into your property.
cues.zh: 对交通的持续担忧，部分是因为人们不想让拥堵拖慢出行，但另一部分也是因为不想让安静、安全、宜人的街道被一堆新汽车或卡车侵占。尽量减少汽车的影响，甚至已经融入郊区住宅的基本设计。郊区的大前院和房屋常与人行道相距10米以上，一个常见理由就是让你离穿过社区的任何交通更远，以避开噪音，以及汽车撞上你房产的可能性。

cues.en: This actually happened to a neighboring house when I was a kid. The suburbs are, in a pretty fundamental way, built on our recognition of the negative effects of traffic and the desire to limit cars in their own neighborhoods. In that sense, we're not so different after all. That's why it's hard to take it seriously when we're accused of being anti-car or against people's freedom to drive. Can someone who enjoys living on a suburban cul-de-sac and who doesn't want denser housing in their neighborhood because of the traffic
cues.zh: 这事我小时候真在邻居家发生过。郊区从根本上是建立在我们对交通负面效应的认识，以及想把汽车限制在自己社区内的愿望之上。从这个意义上说，我们其实没那么不同。所以，当我们被指责反汽车、或反对人们开车的自由时，很难把这话当真。一个喜欢住在郊区死胡同、并且因为交通问题不想让社区更高密度开发的人，

cues.en: really complain about people who live closer to downtown building bike lanes, giving less space to cars, and trying to slow or reduce traffic. These traffic calming barriers in Montreal were installed in 2011 to block cars driving through a school zone. Is this a war on the car? An attack on people's right to drive wherever they want? Because this is functionally the same as a suburban cul-de-sac. Maybe we don't see cul-de-sacs as a limit on freedom because they're built like that from the beginning, while these barriers were added in later. But they do the same thing. They block through traffic.
cues.zh: 真的会抱怨住在更靠近市中心的人修建自行车道、减少汽车空间、试图让交通变慢或减少吗？蒙特利尔这些交通稳静化路障于2011年安装，用来阻止汽车穿过学校区域。这是对汽车的战争吗？是对人们想开去哪儿就开到哪儿的权利的攻击吗？因为这在功能上和郊区死胡同一样。也许我们不把死胡同看作对自由的限制，因为它们从一开始就是这么建的，而这些路障是后来加上的。但它们做的是同一件事：阻挡过境交通。

cues.en: We're making the point that initiatives like traffic calming, bike lanes, and transit priority are the urbanist equivalents to suburban designs and policies, like cul-de-sac, single-leaf zoning, and density restrictions, because they're all meant to manage and limit the effects of cars. There is a major difference though, because the urbanist approach to managing cars is built on providing alternatives and reducing the amount of driving that people have to do, while the suburban approach is based on locking people into driving and increasing overall traffic, but moving it somewhere else for other people to deal with.
cues.zh: 我们要说明的是，交通稳静化、自行车道和公交优先等举措，在城市主义者看来，相当于郊区的设计与政策，比如死胡同、单户住宅区划和密度限制，因为它们都是为了管理和限制汽车的影响。但有一个重大区别：城市主义者管理汽车的思路，建立在提供替代方案、减少人们不得不开车的里程上；而郊区思路则是把人锁死在开车上，增加整体交通量，只是把交通转移到别处，让别人去承受。

cues.en: Montreal's traffic calming barriers aren't actually the same as a suburban cul-de-sac, because a cul-de-sac blocks all traffic modes, creating longer distances and encouraging people to drive. Traffic calming barriers, which you've also seen in Quebec City and Ottawa for example, block cars but continue to allow easy access for people on foot or bike, with technology that could also be built to allow transit to go through.
cues.zh: 蒙特利尔的交通稳静化路障其实和郊区死胡同不同，因为死胡同阻断所有交通方式，拉长出行距离，还鼓励人们开车。交通稳静化路障——你在魁北克城和渥太华也见过——只挡住汽车，但仍让步行者和骑行者方便通行，相关技术也可设计成允许公共交通穿过。

cues.en: The contrast between a completely impermeable cul-de-sac and a selectively impermeable traffic calming setup really shows the difference between urbanism and what we might call suburbanism. But this is more than just road layout. Denser, mixed-use development that puts people close to schools, stores, and jobs can actually get to the root of the traffic problem by making people not have to drive as much, instead of just pushing the driving somewhere else. That is the basic contradiction of North American car-centric suburbia.
cues.zh: 完全无法穿行的死胡同，与选择性阻断穿行的交通稳静化方案形成对比，这真正体现了城市主义与我们可称为郊区主义的区别。但这不只是道路布局的问题。更密集、混合用途的开发让人们更靠近学校、商店和工作地点，能通过减少人们的开车需求，从根源上解决交通问题，而不是只把车流推到别处。这就是北美以汽车为中心的郊区的基本矛盾。

cues.en: If you live in a cul-de-sac or other quiet street in the middle of a residential neighborhood, isolated from businesses and far from your job downtown, you've minimized traffic around your home in immediate neighborhood, but you've maximized the amount of traffic you generate for other people. Whether that's other suburbanites who can't afford the desirable quiet streets within suburbia, or that's people who live in the central city whose neighborhoods you drive through to get to your job, in some cases on highways from the 60s and 70s that demolished large parts of their neighborhood.
cues.zh: 如果你住在死胡同或住宅区中间其他安静街道上，远离商业区，也远离市中心的上班地点，那你把自家周边近邻的交通量降到了最低，却把你给别人带来的交通量推到了最高。无论这些人是负担不起郊区里那些理想安静街道的其他郊区居民，还是住在市中心的人——你开车穿过他们的社区去上班，有时还走的是六七十年代修建、曾拆毁他们社区大片区域的高速公路。

cues.en: Suburbia, at least as we largely know it today, is based on avoiding traffic as much as possible while generating as much traffic as possible. It's anti-car in your own neighborhood, but pro-car through other people's neighborhoods. While this is a critical perspective on North American car-dependent suburban development, our basic point in this video is that we're all more similar than we think.
cues.zh: 至少就我们今天大体所知的郊区而言，它是建立在尽可能避开交通的同时又制造尽可能多交通之上的。它在你自己的社区反汽车，但在别人的社区支持汽车。虽然这是对北美依赖汽车的郊区开发的一种批判视角，但本视频的基本观点是：我们彼此的相似程度超出想象。

cues.en: Almost everyone, whether urban or suburban, recognizes the downsides of cars and wants to manage and limit cars around their home and in their own neighborhoods. Everyone wants their children to be able to play outside safely. No one likes waking up in the middle of the night because of loud cars. What we need is a recognition that urbanist policies like pedestrian streets, bike lanes, transit priority, and traffic calming aren't crazy anti-car aberrations, they're an understandable expression of concerns and preferences that most people have.
cues.zh: 几乎所有人，无论住在城市还是郊区，都认识到汽车的弊端，都想管理和限制自家周围及自己社区里的汽车。每个人都希望孩子能在户外安全玩耍。没人喜欢半夜被吵闹的汽车吵醒。我们需要认识到，步行街、自行车道、公交优先和交通稳静化等城市主义政策，并不是疯狂的反汽车异类，而是对大多数人关切和偏好的合理表达。

cues.en: This video is a call to think in a more productive way about how we can reduce car dependence and overall car traffic, instead of trying to fix the problem by moving it somewhere else for other people to deal with. Don't forget to reduce traffic for everyone and subscribe. We'd like to extend a special thanks to our growing community of patrons.
cues.zh: 这段视频呼吁我们换一种更有效的思路，去思考如何减少汽车依赖和整体车流量，而不是把问题挪到别处、让别人去处理。别忘了为所有人减少交通流量，并订阅本频道。我们要特别感谢不断壮大的赞助者社群。
